This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

01.
2. Heard Mr. S. Tibrewal, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Mr. B.S. Rayaguru,
learned Central Government Counsel appearing for Union of India.
3.

The petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking to quash the order dated 17.02.2023 passed by opposite party no.5 vide Annexure- 14 to the writ petition, by which the grievance of the petitioner was considered and rejected in compliance to the order of this Court dated 05.01.2023 passed in W.P.(C) No. 34992 of 2022.

4. Mr. Tiberwal, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that the reason assigned in the order dated 17.02.2023 is not well justified for which the petitioner has approached this Court in the present writ petition seeking for quashing of the same.

5. Mr. B.S. Rayguru, learned Central Government Counsel appearing for the opposite parties contended that since development work is going on and as such the claim of the petitioner has been considered and by a reasoned order the same has been rejected, therefore, the order impugned need not be interfered with by this Court at this Stage.
6.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after going through the record, it appears that by virtue of the gift deed made by her father, the petitioner owned a piece of land Mouza- Kuruda,
P.S- Balasore Sadar, Khata No 196/380, Plot No. 602/1163 having an area of Ac. 0.160 dec.

Subsequently in the year 2005, the petitioner with a view to convert the land into homestead land,
deposited premium amount of Rs.2400.00 vide RR No. 666150 dated 07.02.2005 before the RI,

Accordingly, ROR was issued in the name of the petitioner having the nature of the land as homestead.
The said plot is situated in a commercial area of Balasore for which the petitioner was willing to make construction over the same for commercial-cum- residential purpose.

While the petitioner was arranging funds to make construction over the said land, a notification under section 3 of the Petroleum and Mineral Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 (P & MP Act. 1962) was issued for acquisition of underground Pipeline by the Indian Oil Corporation Ltd.

entities.text: Petroleum and Mineral Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 (P & MP Act. 1962)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On 28.09.2013 the competent authority issued a letter to the petitioner inviting objection with regard to acquisition of her land.
The petitioner was residing at Mumbai, for which the notice under Section 3 of the P & MP Act, 1962 could not be served on her in time.
The notice was received by the petitioner in the month of April, 2014.

After receipt of the notice dated 28.09.2013 under Annexure-1 petitioner filed an objection on 15.04.2014 as provided under Section 5 of P & MP Act, 1962 before opposite party no.6 along with others specifically stating therein that, her land is a homestead land and she proposed to construct a dwelling house on the said land.
As there is a bar under Section 7 of the Pipeline Act, 1962, no pipeline shall be laid on her land.

But in spite of her objection dated 15.04.2014 and without giving any response to her objection, the authorities on 14.07.2014 issued notification under Section 6(1) of the Pipelines Act to acquire the land of the petitioner.
Even though the petitioner had submitted her objection on 15.04.2014 , but the same has not been considered and the objection so filed was pending before opposite party no.6 for consideration

. On verification,
the petitioner came to know that the opposite parties have published a notification u/s 6(1) of the P & MP Act on 19th July, 2014 for acquisition of her land.
Though notice was issued to the petitioner on 12.08.2014, but the same was delivered to the petitioner in her Mumbai address after lapse of long period.
By that time, the stipulated period had already been expired.
In any case, after the notification was issued, the petitioner moved the authority, but the same having not been considered, the petitioner filed a writ petition bearing W.P.(C) No. 34922 of 2022.
The said writ petition was disposed of vide order dated 05.01.2023 directing the authorities to consider the representation and pass appropriate order in accordance with law.

7. In response to the same, the opposite parties have passed the order under Annexure-14, wherein it has been specifically mentioned that in her representation dated 10/13.10.2022, the petitioner has reiterated the contents of her earlier representation dated 24.06.2022, which have already been replied by the opposite parties vide their communication dated 03.01.2023.

In the said letter it has also been indicated that the IOCL has already given the reply on 12.07.2022 communicating therein that IOCL reserves its right to proceed against the petitioner in accordance with law to recover excess amount paid to her on the basis of the fraud committed by her vis--vis the erroneous determination of compensation amount made in her favour by the competent authority, who had passed the award in question in her favour to the extent of Rs.31,00,000/-.

It has also been clarified that for the purpose of pipeline project, till date the IOCL has utilized only Ac. 0.08 decimal of her land from the acquired user rights pertaining to Ac.
0.11 decmial out of the total area measuring to Ac. 0.16 decimal belonging to the pot in question.

IOCL is authorized and entitled in law to utilize the full stretch of acquired portion of the user rights on the land, i.e. to the extent of Ac. 0.11 decimal as and when the same would be required by the IOCL for the purpose of maintenance of the pipeline for which the petitioner has been paid the compensation amount much more than her legitimate entitlements.
The IOCL shall get no right to Suchitra Das vs Union Of India And Others .....

2 utilize more than Ac. 0.11 decimal of user right of the land belonging to the plot in question.
Therefore, after making a detailed discussion and passing a reasoned order, the claim of the petitioner was rejected.

8. It is contended that since acquisition has been made by following due procedure and the compensation has been paid to the petitioner, which she has also acknowledged, now the question of reverting back to the original position does not arise.

As such, the IOCL has filed Civil Misc. Case No. 01/2023 before the District Judge, Balasore under Section 10 (2) of the P & M.P. Act, 1962 seeking modification of the award of compensation dated 03.10.2016 passed in favour of the petitioner for recovery of the excess amount paid to her on the basis of the fraud committed by her.
The said matter was posted to 16.03.2023 for office report.
The petitioner, if interested may very well contest the said case to redress her grievance, if any.
9. In view of the above, this Court in not inclined to entertain the prayer made in this writ petition.

Thus, the writ petition merits no consideration and the same stands dismissed.
(DR. B.R. SARANGI) Designation: ADR-cum-Addl.
